claims.text: The as-cast Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a favorable strength–ductility balance.
Mobile dislocations interact with local solute atmospheres in the relevant deformation regime.
Removing Co modifies the alloy's stacking-fault energy.
Removing Co modifies the energy landscape for dislocation locking and unlocking.
At low temperatures and slow strain rates, Co removal strengthens solute–dislocation interactions.
At low temperatures and slow strain rates, solute–dislocation interactions promote dislocation locking or dynamic strain aging.
Enhanced dislocation locking increases the yield strength of the Co-free alloy.
Increasing temperature thermally activates dislocation unpinning and recovery.
Increasing strain rate leaves insufficient time for robust solute atmospheres to form and therefore reduces dislocation locking.
Reduced dislocation locking enhances dislocation mobility, recovery, and ductility.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength at low temperatures and low strain rates.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a more pronounced increase in ductility as temperature rises.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show improved ductility at high strain rates through accelerated dislocation unpinning.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution and deformation is primarily dislocation-mediated.
The proposed mechanism does not apply when phase transformations, precipitation, or recrystallization dominate.
An identical temperature-and-strain-rate test matrix for Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi provides the controlled comparison.
The proposed test regime spans approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1 and room temperature to 600–900 °C.

Failure of the Co-free alloy to show higher low-temperature, low-rate yield strength, or failure to observe a corresponding change in locking and solute-atmosphere behavior, would falsify the hypothesis.
